audit_findings.title: Potential $211 million investee-acquisition obligation is absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum disclosed contractual amount of approximately $211.0 million, equal to $2.12 per share and 1.37% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unavoidable net obligation would be deducted in the equity bridge, after recognizing the value of the additional investee interest received.
audit_findings.evidence: The table above also excludes potential obligations related to our investment activities of approximately $211.0 million (based on contractual amounts, excluding working capital adjustments), including arrangements that provide for the potential acquisition of the remaining equity interests in an investee, as well as contingent consideration arrangements.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a contingent arrangement, not a demonstrated present liability. Even treating the entire $211.0 million as an uncompensated claim would reduce values to about $130.09, $153.06, and $180.01 per share in the bear, base, and bull cases. All remain below the $224.59 market price, so it cannot change the present valuation conclusion. A gross deduction may also be inappropriate because payment would acquire additional equity interests.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the investment agreements, identify triggers and settlement timing, value the additional interests acquired, and rerun the bridge using only the present value of any unavoidable net claim.

audit_findings.title: Separately added stakes may double count equity-method earnings already in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Unquantified; each $1 million recurring FY2026 OE error changes base value by approximately $14.05 million, or $0.14 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method earnings embedded in the OE numerator and a separately added stake would count the same economics twice; losses or basis-difference amortization left in OE could instead understate value.
audit_findings.evidence: The investments are subsequently adjusted to recognize the Company's proportionate share of the investees' earnings or losses, distributions received, amortization of basis differences, and impairments, if any, with the impacts on our earnings recorded within Other (income) expense on the Consolidated Statements of Income.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that equity-method results enter Other expense (income), but the supplied record does not show whether they were removed from OE or which investments comprise the $48.7 million bridge addition. FY2026 Other expense, net was $3.5 million, but its undisclosed components prevent measuring the recurring numerator overlap. Because a recurring OE error is capitalized across the forecast and terminal value, materiality cannot be established or dismissed.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2026 and historical Other expense (income), net by investment and adjustment type; map those investments to stakes_net; then rerun OE and all scenarios excluding earnings, losses, amortization, gains, and distributions attributable to separately valued stakes.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash may have unmodeled repatriation tax leakage
audit_findings.magnitude: Tax leakage unquantified; the entire $482.3 million cash bridge equals $4.85 per share and 3.13% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Withholding or remittance taxes would reduce the cash and short-term investments added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: It is not practicable to estimate the additional income taxes and applicable withholding taxes that would be payable on the remittance of such undistributed earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that taxes on remitting foreign earnings cannot be estimated, but it does not establish that the $482.3 million cash balance is trapped or taxable upon access. Even removing the entire cash addition—far more severe than applying tax leakage—would leave the bull value near $177.28 per share, still well below the $224.59 market price. The issue therefore cannot change the current valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Determine cash by entity and jurisdiction, identify amounts already held by the parent or freely deployable locally, calculate applicable withholding and income taxes, and reduce the bridge only by the resulting leakage.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved IRS assessment is an omitted contingent claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $50.0 million principal, equal to $0.50 per share and 0.32% of base equity value; interest and penalties unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse resolution would reduce cash or create a claim deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The IRS adjustments would result in a cumulative tax liability of approximately $ 50.0 million, excluding any interest and penalties, if ultimately assessed.
audit_findings.explanation: The IRS notices and $50.0 million principal exposure are demonstrated, but liability is unresolved and STERIS continues to contest the assessment without a reserve. A full principal deduction would reduce base value from $155.18 to about $154.68 per share and cannot change the conclusion that market price exceeds even bull value. The record does not quantify interest and penalties, but supplies no evidence that they approach the $42.46-per-share gap between market price and bull value.
audit_findings.action: Update the Tax Court status, compute statutory interest and potential penalties through the valuation date, assess outcome probabilities with tax counsel, and rerun the bridge if the probability-weighted claim becomes significant.

audit_findings.title: Historical OE may mix the retained business with disposed Dental cash flows
audit_findings.magnitude: Unquantified net effect; filed Dental amounts include $115.2 million of FY2024 D&A and capital expenditures of $9.2 million in FY2024 and $0.4 million in FY2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Dental D&A, capital spending, and working-capital movements remaining in historical cash-flow data could distort historical OE and therefore the volatility assessment and selected growth case.
audit_findings.evidence: Our Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows include the financial results of the Dental segment through the date of sale on May 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing proves that consolidated cash flows included Dental through May 31, 2024, but it does not prove that the supplied OE series failed to remove those amounts. The disclosed D&A and capital expenditures do not provide the full working-capital or other cash-flow adjustment needed to calculate the error. The FY2026 anchor is post-disposal, but distorted history could influence growth selection; the scenario spread is $49.92 per share, making that judgment potentially material.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every affected historical OE year from continuing-operation schedules, removing Dental D&A, capex, working capital, sale-related items, and other adjustments; then reassess the too-hard flag and rerun growth scenarios without changing the FY2026 actual anchor unless a separate anchor error is found.

audit_findings.title: Maintenance capital requirements may be understated
audit_findings.magnitude: Unquantified; FY2026 total capital expenditures were $369.0 million and D&A was $486.5 million, while each $1 million recurring OE overstatement changes base value by approximately $14.05 million, or $0.14 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring replacement, cobalt-60, compliance, facility-maintenance, or technology spending omitted from the maintenance-capex deduction would overstate the $1,060.5 million OE anchor and every forecast and terminal cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: In fiscal 2027, we plan to continue to invest in facility expansions, particularly within our Healthcare and AST segments, and in ongoing maintenance for existing facilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes a substantial capital program and planned ongoing maintenance, but does not disclose the maintenance-versus-growth split embedded in OE. It therefore does not demonstrate an error or quantify one. Because any recurring shortfall is capitalized through the forecast and terminal value, a relatively modest annual misclassification could materially affect value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the FY2026 maintenance deduction to project-level capital expenditures, including facility upkeep, cobalt-60 replacement, regulatory spending, recurring capacity replacement, and the technology program; separate genuinely incremental growth projects and rerun all scenarios using the supported recurring maintenance amount.
